title: Why Yawning Is Contagious (Even Between Dogs and Humans!) & Why Morning Stretching Feels Like a Mini-High — Robert Provine's contagious-yawning ethology (45–60% video contagion, 30% yawn / 75% urge just from reading text), Andrew Gallup's forehead ice-pack drop (9% vs. 45%) & inverted-U thermal window (Tucson 22 vs. 37 °C, PMID 21960970; Vienna 1.4 vs. 19.4 °C, PMID 24721675; rat cortical cooling, PMID 21031034); One Medicine canine yawn contagion (Joly-Mascheroni 2008: 21/29 = 72.4% vs. 0%; Romero 2013 owner bias & flat HR; Neilands 2020 Bayesian critique); PVN D2R -> NO -> OXTR (PDB 7JVR, 7RYC) & morning pandiculation inside trimeric Piezo2 (PDB 6KG7).

teenKit.tldr: Just reading or hearing about a yawn can physically hijack your jaw because yawning acts as an ancient evolutionary air-conditioner that cools your brain down. When your brain gets too warm, your nervous system triggers a massive involuntary stretch and intake of cool air to restore peak mental performance.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding why we yawn and stretch reveals that our bodies use surprisingly low-tech thermal physics to keep our brains running smoothly across both humans and animals.
keyTakeaways: Just reading about yawning triggers a physical urge in 75% of people and makes 30% actually yawn, proving how easily your brain can be visually or mentally hacked.
Andrew Gallup's research shows yawning is actually a brain-cooling mechanism; putting an ice-pack on your forehead drops contagious yawning from 45% down to 9%.
Morning stretching, or pandiculation, activates Piezo2 proteins in your body to wake up your muscles and reset your nervous system after a long sleep.

quiz.question: According to Robert Provine's studies, what percentage of people report an urge to yawn simply from reading text about yawning?
quiz.explanation: Provine found that while 30% of people physically yawn from reading text, an incredible 75% feel the active urge to do so.

quiz.question: What happens to contagious yawning if you place an ice pack on someone's forehead before they watch a yawn video?
options: It doubles because of the cold shock
quiz.explanation: Cooling the forehead drops contagious yawning from 45% to 9% because the brain no longer needs thermal relief.

quiz.question: What is the primary biological function of spontaneous yawning according to the research discussed?
options: To cool down an overheated brain
To increase lung capacity for running
To signal that it is time to eat
quiz.explanation: Yawning functions as an evolutionary brain-cooling mechanism that helps regulate internal neural temperature during arousal transitions.
